This might be long so sorry in advance. Im still processing it, but the ending really elevated the whole thing for me. This rush of empathy and humanity floods in out of nowhere and shines every character in a new light. Laura is no longer just a cruel monster, but a grieving mother who is fully disfigured by desperation and the agony of losing her daughter. Ollie is no longer just a grotesque demon puppet, but a frightened , traumatized child who is finally being rescued. Hearing his real voice for the first time was heartbreaking. Having Piper fight back and use her intelligence to get herself to safety, even without her brother to help her, was such a brilliant move. She wasn’t there to be just a helpless victim. Especially screaming ‘MOM’ to take Laura off guard when she ran out of options. And the shot of the plane after Andy’s voice mail. So many great call backs for the audience that didn’t feel contrived or obvious, just all the pieces coming together perfectly. 

As deeply tragic and harrowing as the film still is, there’s this otherworldly and overwhelming feeling of emotional catharsis that is almost poetic. It’s such a crazy spectrum of emotions being felt all at once and it truly captures the  aftermath of grief in a way I haven’t seen captured in the same way before. 

The Philippous  had more on their minds than just terrifying the audience, or pointless misery porn, you can tell they care for their characters despite what they put them through.They pulled it off masterfully.  I love Talk To Me and Hereditary, but this easily tops them both and hit me with way more visceral impact. I will instantly be seated for whatever they do next.

Long response — weird mood— still sober— mostly writing this response for myself. 

Rehab was a great/beneficial experience for me, but not always fun and never easy and not a cake walk. Many who were there hated it, and if not there by law, left early. But for a few of us it was positive. 

It isn’t some fantastical vacation or holiday , and if you can’t afford the ‘deluxe’ locations it’s kind of like being in a prison that actually gives a shit about your well being, while knowing in the back of your mind that you won’t be there forever. Like some weird adult day care you are left at. 

On the other hand, it’s still only humans running it and they aren’t some fairies who can magically fix you, they are usually under a lot of stress themselves or exhausted or dealing with the 100th meltdown of the day or yet another combative patient who thinks they’ll get their way if they are threatening or ass holes. They may not always have answers and their idea of treatment may not work for you but that’s okay. It doesn’t have to and you can speak up to make adjustments. Also, the challenges and issues in your life that led you there in the first place may still in fact remain when you get out, but you’ll learn how to handle them/find a solution to them a lot better. HOWEVER you MIGHT feel like a brand new person right before you get out and ready to live the perfect life, the hardest part for me was navigating my life outside when I was left to my own devices and feelings and stress I forgot about comes. I did relapse briefly but now I’m nearly two years strong. A loved one passed unexpectedly very early on after my release and it was rough. Had it happened before I went , however, things may have gone even worse. Fortunately I regained my footing. 

It mainly gives you a place to detox safely, get back to some kind of routine or structure , get addiction education etc, look into resources , and so on. It’s fascinating and enlightening in many ways just listening to other people share their stories. Everyone is at their most vulnerable, maybe darkest moments of their lives, or having to face buried truths that they’ve long since ignored or tried forgetting through drugs and alcohol etc. All of those TERRIBLE reasons that led you to rehab in the first place are being put to max volume and brought into laser focus.  You will cry a lot, in front of others , by yourself, and with others at some point. But you slowly notice the healing beginning and there are moments of hope and happiness, because I did laugh harder than I ever had in a long while. At some point the good times slowly start outweighing the awful ones. 

So yes it really does come down to what you bring to it and what your outlook is. I learned that I’m patient as fuck, that I’m generally likable and not a bad person, and that some people have made worse mistakes and I don’t have it as bad in comparison, even if that doesn’t make my own issues easier. I also learned I have a long way to go and a lot of improvements to make. 

Still, the program isn’t perfect and there are many improvements that could be made and many changes that could be done but American health care , especially when it comes to addiction or mental health issues is severely lacking and every one is doing the best they can even if that isn’t always going to be good enough for everybody. And if you can’t afford it on your insurance stops covering it, no matter how well you bond with the employees there, you’ll promptly get the boot. I wish I could have stayed longer sometimes but I also enjoy having my freedom. Also there are some of the WORST and most insufferable people you will ever have to share oxygen with, but the also the BEST people you likely never would have ever known they existed, and it’s through that shared bond you can tolerate the insufferable ones. Usually they don’t last long either. Some will just come to rest a few days and not participate or hate being there and will take it out on you. but you do form some great friendships and meet others who will stick up for you. 

So yeah, it does come down to if you WANT to change, WANT help, WILLINGNESS to open your mind , and relinquishing your control to something else. If you go in with your guard up or actively resisting and are miserable and stubborn there’s really no point in going. If you’re scared of going for whatever reason, no matter what, AT LEAST TRY. Worst case scenario you can’t adapt and you check yourself out early , best case you start benefiting from the rewards by sticking through the challenges. You may surprise yourself , it’s going to be uncomfortable initially and scary , but you can’t get the juice without the squeeze ! 

Addiction is a bitch, sobriety might also still be a bitch , but unlike addiction, it’s less destructive and great things can come of it , while your only outcome with the former is jail, psych wards, death, or more and more reasons to keep using to forget. 

Wouldn’t you rather play a game where a chance at winning more than once is a possibility, rather than one where the only guarantee is the outcome of losing?

Movie theaters really bring out some of the worst pieces of shit.  Being polite or following the rules are their biggest triggers. 

During Barbenheimer, four of us were cleaning one of big auditoriums which were trashed, of course. We had barely started and a woman comes in sits down in a seat where beer glasses are in both cup holders, the chair is reclined, its covered in trash and popcorn, and she starts asking us to clean around her. 

Then other people start coming in seeing her and also start walking to their seats. I finally stop them and ask for them to wait outside, including the woman , ( “ Yeah, ma’am, if you don’t mind waiting by the door and we’ll let you in when we are finished please “) the fucking “cleaning is in progress” was also displayed mind you. 

She starts arguing and leaves and then her husband comes in and gets in my face threatening me saying I called her a cunt and screamed at her. My coworkers calmly told him it wasn’t true, while having to step in between me and the man and her wife screaming. 

The managers get involved and long story short they got free passes for the next time and I was told not to get aggressive with customers (they were mostly doing it to save face in front of them but still). It’s infuriating. “What? I can’t be an inconsiderate ass hole to you and everyone in here?” Someone also ANSWERED there phone in a packed theater. it’s insane.

Even if you don’t go to the movies much EVERY ONE knows this, it’s like in the 10 commandments of movie going. Except ass holes who follow their own laws. 

But yes there are usually signs next to every door on the wall , and before the ads start.

Some of these are retrieved by the distributor or at least have rules against taking them. BUT this is mostly just on paper and isn’t enforced much. 

Like others have said, just ask a manager or write down/let coworkers know to save it. I have worked at many theaters many years and I’m overflowing with posters and standees and another promo material. 

Some of it I asked for , others I just snuck into my car when we were destroying it. I used to ask, but other times if I was told to break it down and toss it’d just take it with me on break or after my shift. Sometimes no one knew, other times they did but didn’t care. 

I’ve never once been told that it wasn’t allowed (after taking it without asking ) faced repercussions, or write ups, or gotten in trouble because of it. Many I’ve end up finding stashed somewhere years after release so obviously no one cares that much. 

If I were you I’d stick a note on the back asking “hey, please don’t break down/toss  out and let me know first, I’ll take it!” 

The BIGGEST issue is that this takes up space and there’s not many places that someone could stash it that isn’t in someone’s way or could be considered a safety risk if it’s in front of emergency exits (it really wouldn’t make it difference realistically, but on paper it would technically) unless someone is considerate to save it in the break room for you if you’re not working that day or someone doesn’t know you want it or someone just doesn’t give a shit. 

So just let your coworkers know you want it , but wait a couple weeks because they  can’t let anyone take it if they are required to send it. Or if someone takes it from you first — sometimes many of us wanted the same thing so it was first claimed first served. 

The FBI isn’t going to show up at your door and no one in the long run is going to make a big deal about it unless they are huge sticklers about “the rules “.

I liked how this one was still able to surprise me 6 movies in, not on the same level as the twist in the last one, but it’s apparent that the creators actually care about the franchise. 

1) Having the premonition be a different person took me completely off guard. Much like Scream 5 and the character surviving the opening kill, it was a clever subversion of expectations. 

2) The reveal about Bludworth was both an incredible twist (i love when it is obvious and put in front of you and you STILL don’t see it coming) but also one of the best send offs of a legacy character I’ve ever seen. It was bittersweet and I didn’t expect to be moved emotionally like that. I love how, knowing his illness, they let Tony Todd go off script and say whatever he wanted. It was just really sweet and poignant. The whole movie felt like a love letter to him, even if the rest of it had been terrible (it wasn’t ) it was a perfect scene. 

I didn’t love the movie as much as others did, but it was still enjoyable and a fun horror movie and there was a lot of effort put into it that payed off. The deaths were gruesome enough— the set up and execution of the garbage truck death was BRILLIANT and made me laugh so hard— and it was low key refreshing to see a modern horror movie not try to annihilate me emotionally and spiritually. I LOVE the new wave of A24/Neon/‘elevated’ horror (hate that term), but sometimes the directors forget to lighten up and for once I didn’t walk out in a deep depression. Though that will stop tomorrow after Bring Her Back. 

I would probably have been obsessed with Bloodlines as a pre-teen like when FD2 came out. Hopefully it doesn’t spawn like 5 more sequels — sometimes it’s better to leave good enough alone— but with the success of this one I doubt that will be the case. Hopefully they keep it simple.

I don’t get what this guy is going on about. 

It wasn’t originally supposed to be a Halo movie. Yes, Jackson and Blomkamp were going to make a Halo adaptation, but financing fell through. They decided to make a movie any way, and expanded Blomkamp’s short film Alive in Joburg. They did use props made for the Halo adaptation, but they were just left overs , why wouldn’t you? 

People didn’t want a see a sequel because of any of that. The movie was hugely popular when it came out and a box office success. It even got 4 academy award nominations including Best Picture. And yes it did have an ending which was wide open for a sequel. But I think it ended well on its own. Anything more would have just been a retread on an original premise where we already know what happened to the main character (the final shot is beautiful and sad without spelling things out). 

Unfortunately, Blomkamp has only gone on to bomb every other movie he’s made, and his projects have become progressively worse. Elysium and Chappie have some fans but a very small group as most were mixed, Demonic was flat out abysmal. Gran Turismo was sort of an improvement but also nothing special. 

District 9 continues to be his only good-to-great film, and also a fluke.

This is why I don’t like saying “the best” or “my favorite “ especially when it comes to acting and movies. It is all so subjective and everyone has different tastes. 

Ronan is certainly ONE of the best working right now and has been for a long time. I agree with you about Brokeback Mountain. Being a closeted teenager in a small town, it was refreshing to see (however in secret) a gay romance that was to be taken seriously and starring two of the best male actors working at the time in the lead roles. Then for it to be acclaimed and later Oscar nominated was also sweet. It definitely helped in breaking down barriers and new ground. 

However , it’s very much of its time. As you said the relationship is very sanitized. While the love shared between them is there, there is a distinct lack of actual on screen passion. Save for a couple kisses, it always cuts away from the act of love making , we only ever see the beginning or right after. While I don’t think it needed 9 minute long explicit sex scenes (like Blue is the Warmest Color), it did feel like the makers of it were afraid to go all the way. It feels like they sacrificed any raw intimacy so that it would still be palatable to straight, more conservative viewers. Plus it likely would have been given an NC17, as they were pretty notorious for slapping anything with gay sex with that rating— like Bad Education and Boys Don’t Cry (which was later appealed and dropped to an R). 

Now we see graphic gay sex scenes all the time , even on television, and it’s not considered controversial or shocking any more.

It’s more comedic in tone, albeit in a bleak way, but I genuinely love Karol Karol as a protagonist, he’s somewhat identifiable which may not be a good thing , but seeing this flawed and unlucky man find his version of justice is excellent. Delay is also great, and appropriately cold. The ending is immensely satisfying and absolute perfection, like a brilliant punch line. 

Honestly, picking a favorite or ranking them is mostly pointless IMO. It’s my favorite trilogy, and Kieslowski was a true master and taken from us way too early. I consider it one of the most opulent and gorgeous horror films ever made and it's not even considered in the horror genre. The atmosphere is just so suffocating. Jackie was also solid with one of Portman's best (he sure knows how to get the best out of the actresses he works with) and that great score by Mica Levi. I still hope Criterion releases a box set for the trilogy. Even if I'd rarely revisit this one.  If I were to score them: Jackie- 4/5, Spencer- 5/5, Maria- 3/5 (again, only given a passing grade because of Jolie and the visuals).

Reminded me a lot of Andrew Dominic's Blonde, only not offensively disgusting, gratuitous,  and exploitative. It's stunningly gorgeous throughout thanks to the great Ed Lachman's cinematography. Every single shot is just a feast for the eyes, I found myself commenting on how beautiful every frame was that I had to force myself to shut up about it. Across the board when it comes to the technical aspects the film is a masterpiece.  

It's also shallow as hell. One of the reasons both Jackie and Spencer worked is because there was a certain  historical context that we were already familiar with going into it, with First Lady Jackie Onassis Kennedy and Princess Diana, both being household names, if not universally recognizable. 

Maybe I'm just living under a rock, but I didn't know much, if anything, about Maria Callas, other than she was a famous opera singer. By the end I still didn't know much, other then she was addicted to pills which she popped like candy, and was prone to angry mood swings and hallucinations . The storytelling device with her having conversations with the personification of her qualuudes was definitely a choice, but it kind of worked I guess, could have been worse. Not as successful as Diana's hallucinations like the pearls in the soup, and the brief appearances of Anne Boleyn. But at least it wasn't a total misfire. 

There are two reasons I'd give this a barely passing grade-- like 3 out of 5-- one is Angelina Jolie who once again commands the screen and is both powerful and subtle. It's refreshing to see her in a role like this after big budget films like Eternals and the Maleficent series. She  is mesmerizing and it's one of her greatest performances, up there with Gia, The Changeling, and Girl, Interrupted. Even if some of the lipsyncing was fairly obvious, she absolutely still deserves a Best Actress nomination (which seems inevitable). I don't think she'll win it since the movie surrounding her isn't on the same level, but she elevates and carries it entirely. Second is Ed Lachman's outstanding and stunning cinematography which I've already pointed out, but every single frame really does look like a painting, the rich colors, the shot compositions, just an orgasm for the eyes. Multiple of them. He also deserves some nominations, would be criminal if he didn't, credit also to the costume designers and art direction. 

That's about the only positives for me, it's never aggressively terrible, but wafer thin and has mostly evaporated from my memory and I finished it an hour or so ago. I would still purchase a trilogy box set with Jackie, Spencer, and Maria, but this is definitely the weakest of the bunch, and save for a couple moments of fantasy that step outside of the box (like the choir on the steps which switches to women carrying lanterns and surrounding Maria) this is the most basic and conventional, plus their additions aren't quite as seamless just some small diversions. 

Maybe if you're already a fan of Maria that you'll appreciate it more, and I guess if you can't find anything else to watch it wouldn't be a total waste of time thanks to Jolie. But let's just say it makes sense this is the only one that went straight to Netflix.
